items.title: The First Christmas Card (1846) copy
items.depicts: Black-and-white photograph of a printed page reproducing the Cole/Horsley card. You can see the rustic trellis frame, the family round the table raising glasses in the centre, feeding the hungry on the left and clothing the poor on the right. The banner reads 'A MERRY CHRISTMAS AND A HAPPY NEW YEAR TO YOU', with 'To ...' and 'From ...' lines and the imprint 'Published at Summerly's Home Treasury Office, 12 Old Bond Street, London'. The printed caption under the card reads 'THE FIRST CHRISTMAS CARD (1846), DESIGNED BY J. C. HORSLEY, R.A., FOR SIR HENRY COLE'. There is a black negative border and a line of book text at the top.
items.evidence: LoC record 2016850925: title 'The First Christmas Card (1846) copy'; '1 negative : glass ; 5 x 7 in. or smaller'; 'Title from unverified data provided by the National Photo Company on the negative or negative sleeve'; reproduction no. LC-DIG-npcc-27613. This is NOT an 1843 original. It is a 20th-century National Photo Company copy negative of a printed reproduction (book or magazine page), and the 1846 date in its caption is wrong.
items.licence: Library of Congress: 'No known restrictions on publication.' (National Photo Company Collection)

items.title: The first Christmas card, commissioned by Henry Cole (collection Dr. Alan Huggins)
items.date: 1843 (per Commons; not verified by an institution)
items.depicts: Colour (hand-coloured) Cole/Horsley card in warm browns, with a blue dress on the right. Same design: a family toasting at the table, a figure feeding the poor on the left, a woman clothing a child on the right, and a pink banner reading 'A MERRY CHRISTMAS AND A HAPPY NEW YEAR TO YOU'. It is handwritten 'To Mrs Price' and 'From F. C. Hardy' (my reading of the script) and carries the Summerly's Home Treasury Office imprint. The image is a scan of a magazine halftone, so a printing screen is visible at full size.
items.evidence: Commons File:FirstX-MasPostcard1843.jpg. Description: 'The first Christmas card, commissioned by Henry Cole (collection Dr. Alan Huggins)'. Source: 'Philatelie - Das Sammlermagazin des Bundes Deutscher Philatelisten, Edition 309 of March 2003, page 54'. Author: John Callcott Horsley. Commons calls it an 1843 copy in a private collection, but no museum record confirms that it is the 1843 printing. LAST-RESORT SOURCE: the photograph comes from a 2003 German magazine. Downloaded as the 1920px thumbnail (original 2881x1833).
items.licence: Commons: PD-old-70 (Horsley d. 1903) + CC Public Domain Mark 1.0. The underlying 1843 work is PD everywhere. The faithful 2D reproduction attracts no new rights in the US (Bridgeman) or in Germany (s.68 UrhG, since 2021). The Commons page lacks a US PD tag. Use with this caveat; the LoC copy above is the cleanly licensed one.

items.title: Henry Cole Esqr., evecutive commisioner
items.depicts: Wood-engraved half-length portrait of Henry Cole in his forties, with curly hair, a high collar and cravat, and a hand tucked into his coat. The printed caption reads 'HENRY COLE, ESQ., Executive Commissioner.' The running head reads '[...]DON ALMANACK FOR 1852'. It is a cut-out page on cream paper with some text showing through. An NLW colour/scale target along the bottom needs cropping out.
items.evidence: NLW IIIF manifest: label 'Henry Cole Esqr., evecutive commisioner'; Date '1852'; '1 print : wood engraving, b&w; 138 x 101 mm.'; description 'Civil servant. Director of the South Kensington Museum.'; Welsh Portrait Collection PD01043. The sitter is clearly Sir Henry Cole: he was Executive Commissioner of the Great Exhibition of 1851, and the record names the South Kensington Museum.
items.licence: Public Domain Mark 1.0 (license field in the National Library of Wales IIIF manifest); attribution: Llyfrgell Genedlaethol Cymru - The National Library of Wales

items.title: [John Callcott Horsley]
items.depicts: Sepia carte-de-visite of John Callcott Horsley in middle age. It is a head-and-shoulders portrait with side-whiskers, a wing collar and a large bow tie. On the cream mount he has signed 'J. C. Horsley R.A.' and written 'Kensington June 9th 1871'. The printed studio line reads 'JOHN WATKINS, PHOTO / 34 PARLIAMENT ST'.
items.evidence: The Met 1970.659.420: '[John Callcott Horsley]', John and Charles Watkins (British, active 1867-71), albumen silver print, carte-de-visite, The Albert Ten Eyck Gardner Collection. The Met dates it to the 1860s, but the handwritten inscription on the mount says June 1871.

items.title: [Full page of The Illustrated London News, Christmas Supplement, 1848: The Christmas Holly Cart; Fetching home the Christmas dinner]
items.depicts: A full ILN page (p. 408, 'Christmas Supplement, 1848'). The top engraving, 'The Christmas Holly Cart - drawn by Foster', shows a donkey cart heaped with holly in a snowy street of terraced townhouses, with children and a seller. The bottom engraving, 'Fetching home the Christmas dinner - drawn by Leech', shows a crowd of Londoners carrying steaming dishes out of a baker's shop marked 'BAKER J. RUSK', with a 'Christmas Ale' sign. Columns of text sit between the two. Low resolution: each scene is about 950 px wide.
items.evidence: LoC record 2005696288: 'Illus. in: The Illustrated London News, 1848.'; caption-card tracings 'Street vendors; Gt. Brit. Hist. 1848; Holidays Christmas'; LC-USZ62-53386 (b&w film copy neg.).
items.licence: Library of Congress: 'No known restrictions on publication.'

items.title: Street scene in London--winter evening / Ts. Nast.
items.depicts: Wood engraving of a snowy London street at dusk. On the left is a 'HOT ... SOUP' and 'JOINTS' eating-house front, with a roast-chestnut brazier. Ragged children and a crossing-sweeper with a broom mix with top-hatted gentlemen and ladies, and snow lies on the rooftops behind. The page border shows 'HARPER'S WEEKLY' and the caption 'STREET SCENE IN LONDON - WINTER EVENING'. Low resolution.
items.evidence: LoC record 90707481: 'Street scene in London--winter evening / Ts. Nast.'; '1 print : wood engraving.'; 'Illus. in: Harper's weekly, 1859 April 2, p. 212.'; LC-USZ62-99301.
items.licence: Library of Congress: 'No known restrictions on publication.'

items.title: Christmas tree at Windsor Castle / drawn by J.L. Williams.
items.depicts: The famous ILN engraving: Queen Victoria, Prince Albert, the Duchess of Kent and the royal children around a candle-lit, ornament-laden Christmas tree on a table. It sits in an oval inside an elaborate ornamental frame of game, poultry, vignettes and a sleigh medallion. Full page with the bound-volume edge visible.
items.evidence: LoC record 96522234: 'Christmas tree at Windsor Castle / drawn by J.L. Williams.'; '1 print : wood engraving.'; 'Illus. in: The Illustrated London news, Christmas supplement, 1848, p. 409.'; LC-USZ62-117376. The setting is Windsor, not London.
items.licence: Library of Congress: 'No known restrictions on publication.'

items.title: Unused block of four "Penny Black" postage stamps of Queen Victoria
items.depicts: Sharp, close-up block of four Penny Black stamps with Queen Victoria's profile, 'POSTAGE' at the top, 'ONE PENNY.' at the bottom and corner letters B C / B D / C C / C D, on a black mount.
items.evidence: The Met 2002.236.1: 'Unused block of four "Penny Black" postage stamps of Queen Victoria'; William Wyon (British, 1795-1851); engraving printed in black ink on paper; issued May 6, 1840.

items.title: 1p Mulready first day cover
items.depicts: A used Mulready one-penny envelope on cream paper. Mulready's allegorical design shows Britannia sending winged messengers to the world, with figures reading letters in the lower corners. It is addressed in ink to 'Miss Crowfoot, Beccles, Suffolk' and cancelled with a red Maltese Cross. 'POSTAGE ONE PENNY', 'W. MULREADY R.A.' and 'JOHN THOMPSON' are printed along the bottom.
items.evidence: Smithsonian National Postal Museum 0.205561.2: '1p Mulready first day cover'; Date 'May 6, 1840'; 'one penny Mulready first day cover with red Maltese Cross postmark'; type 'Covers & Associated Letters'. Henry Cole's role in commissioning the Mulready design is general history and is not stated in this record.

items.title: Christmas
items.depicts: Small chromolithographed Christmas card with a red ornamental border. A boy in a straw hat and purple coat pushes a cart heaped with holly in the snow, with a robin in a blue scarf in harness. Behind them are a snowy brick wall, a Gothic window and a wooden door. The motto reads 'BUY MY HOLLY GREEN AND GAY, TO DECK YOUR WALLS ON CHRISTMAS DAY', with small imprints 'M.W. & Co.' and 'ENT. STA. HALL'.
items.evidence: The Met 1981.1138.838: title 'Christmas', 1874, Anonymous, 'White card, chromolithography', classification Ephemera (objectName 'Valentine'), Gift of Mrs. Richard Riddell. The 'M.W. & Co.' imprint is probably Marcus Ward & Co., but the record does not say so. 'Ent. Sta. Hall' (Entered at Stationers' Hall) points to a British publisher.

items.title: A doctor's front door, with a chimney sweep, in the snow. Chromolithograph by John Leighton ("Luke Limner").
items.depicts: Victorian Christmas card: a sooty young chimney sweep with his brush shivers and calls out on the snowy doorstep of a green front door. The door has a brass lion knocker and plates reading 'Dr SNORE', 'KNOCK AND RING', 'PATIENTS' and 'SERVANTS', and a soot bag lies in the snow. Along the bottom: 'A MERRY CHRISTMAS AND A HAPPY NEW YEAR.' Modest resolution.
items.evidence: Wellcome Collection 25361i (work k7f4q5v7): '1 print : chromolithograph ; sheet 12.3 x 9 cm'; lettering 'Dr Snore ; patients ; knock and ring ; servants ; a merry Christmas and a happy new year.'; note 'Possibly intended as a visual pun: "sweep in the snow"'.
items.licence: Public Domain Mark (Wellcome Collection, licence id 'pdm')

items.title: Christmas Greeting
items.depicts: Warm chromolithographed card: four children dressed as three cooks in white caps and a kitchen maid play in a brick kitchen with a glowing hearth, copper pans and stacked plates. 'A HAPPY CHRISTMAS' is printed at the top.
items.evidence: Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum 1961-105-58: 'Christmas Greeting', ca. 1890, 'Children are seen busy in a kitchen. They are dressed as three cooks and a kitchen maid. At top: "A Happy Christmas".'; chromolithograph on paper, 7.1 x 10.8 cm; made in USA; Gift of Hamill and Barker.

items.title: A child holds a large bunch of holly and two others watch as a young woman stands on a chair to reach the picture she is decorating for Christmas. Colour process print.
items.depicts: Cozy coloured print in an oval vignette. A girl in a yellow dress stands on a red upholstered chair, hanging holly over a framed portrait in a wood-panelled room. A boy holds up more holly and two small girls watch, one with berries in her apron. The worn card mount has a marbled border.
items.evidence: Wellcome Collection 32640i (work rhv8bsd6): '1 print : process print'. The catalogue gives no date or maker.
items.licence: Public Domain Mark (Wellcome Collection, licence id 'pdm')

items.title: Christmas-Time, The Blodgett Family
items.depicts: Warm, dark oil painting of a wood-panelled parlour at Christmas. A fire glows in the hearth at the left, and the father stands smiling at a little girl in a white dress with a pink sash. The mother sits by a red-clothed table where a boy shows off a toy and an older girl leans on the table, with a small Christmas tree and a wreath at the right and a tall window at the left. The image includes the frame edge.
items.evidence: The Met 1983.486: 'Christmas-Time, The Blodgett Family', 1864, Eastman Johnson (American, 1824-1906), oil on canvas, 30 x 25 in., Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Stephen Whitney Blodgett. This is an AMERICAN (New York) family, not British.

notes: subject_box = normalized [left, top, right, bottom]. 14 stills, each in its own folder with meta.json (helper downloads also keep source.tif masters). FIRST CARD: no commercial-use high-res colour scan of an 1843 original was found from a US or open museum. The V&A, British Library, Postal Museum and Dickens Museum copies are UK/non-commercial or unlicensed, and the Commons files ColeXmascard.jpg and Firstchristmascard.jpg derive from V&A/BL images ('Images may be reproduced only with written permission of V&A Images'), so they were rejected. The LoC Rare Book copy (2019 LoC blog) is not digitized on loc.gov. The cleanly licensed item is the LoC National Photo Company copy negative. It is a b&w photo of a printed reproduction, captioned '1846' in error, and is NOT an 1843 printing. The colour item is a Commons last resort, a magazine-halftone scan of a privately owned copy that Commons calls 1843 (unverified). Rejected: LoC 'Henry Cole' carte de visite 2022676796 (an American sitter photographed in Newark NJ, not Sir Henry Cole); LoC '[Mr. Fezziwig's Ball]' 1843 Leech (rights 'not evaluated', so unclear); Science Museum, NPG London and British Museum Cole portraits (non-commercial). Low-res warnings: the ILN 1848 page (993x1536) and the Nast 1859 street scene (1536x965) are LoC film-copy scans only. The Blodgett painting and the Cooper Hewitt card are American. The Windsor tree is Windsor, not London.
